top_choice_rationale: P002 pairs two mature, measurement-driven achievements that are scientifically unrelated and fit exactly three names: the optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye), reproduced across independent laboratories at the 10^-18 level, and the discovery of a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux with IceCube, established in several independent channels. The weak point is the single-name attribution for IceCube, which rests on a conceiver-and-leader claim; if that cannot be defended, P003 (the lattice clock alone) is the clean, well-attributed fallback, ranked ahead of P001, whose superconducting mechanism is unsettled and whose field is under a decade old. A prize is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: B002 (IceCube) is in my own field of astroparticle physics at KTH, though my profile documents no tie to IceCube or Halzen (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur are separate collaborations); I have no documented connection to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, so no recusal is apparent from the profile.
